observations: Photo 0 shows a yellow in-line diesel engine block mounted on a stand, with fuel filter housing, wiring harness, and various brackets attached.
Photo 1 shows a close-up of the top valve cover; a stamped/molded plate on the cover reads partial lettering consistent with 'CAT' and 'C9'.
No turbocharger, flywheel housing, oil pan, or full front/rear view is visible in either photo.
A watermark reading 'DNL EQUIPMENT SALES AND ...' appears across both photos — this is the seller's own branding, not proof of the item's condition or completeness.
Engine surfaces show grime, oxidation, and grease residue typical of a used, non-running industrial engine.
No serial number plate or ID tag is clearly legible in either photo.

claims.evidence: Photos show only the block, valve cover, and some ancillary parts; no view of turbo, flywheel, oil pan, or full engine perimeter to confirm completeness.
No start-up video, compression test, or oil/coolant check shown; cannot confirm mechanical condition from static photos.

risks.risk: Engine may be missing major components (turbo, flywheel housing, oil pan, injectors) not visible in the two photos.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree walk-around photos/video showing front, rear, underside, and intake/exhaust manifolds.
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete, missing standard accessories

risks.risk: Internal condition (cylinders, bearings, crankshaft) unknown; could be seized, cracked block, or worn out.
risks.proof: Video of engine being turned over or started, or a borescope/compression test result.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for parts only

risks.risk: Exact model variant (C9 vs C9.3, horsepower rating) not confirmed by a clear serial/data plate.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine's official CAT data plate with serial and model number.
risks.if_unproven: priced at base C9 parts-engine tier without horsepower premium

risks.risk: Corrosion or water damage suggested by surface grime could indicate prolonged outdoor storage.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of cylinder bores, oil fill, and coolant passages.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the CAT data/serial plate with full engine model and serial number.
Full exterior walk-around video showing all four sides, top, and underside of the engine.
Video of the engine being manually turned over or started to show it is not seized.
Close-up photos of cylinder head, oil pan, and turbo mounting area to confirm completeness.
response.reason: The engine is identifiable by type and partial brand/model marking as a Caterpillar C9 diesel engine sold for parts, but completeness and working condition are unverified, so it must be priced at the worst-case parts/non-running tier until further proof is given.
